author: beaver state news
title: New York investigators find improper charges in Nissan lease buyouts at dealerships
text:
New York investigators said on Jun. 17 that several Nissan dealerships added unauthorized charges to lease buyouts, resulting in unexpected costs for customers. The investigation found that what should have been a straightforward process was complicated by hidden fees and questionable repair bills, including a $2,563 charge for electrical tape valued at only 8 cents.
The New York Attorney General’s office reviewed nearly 10,000 lease buyout transactions and found improper charges in more than 3,000 cases. As a result of the findings, more than $1 million in penalties have been imposed against 15 dealerships. Customers have received over $4.5 million in refunds so far, with more than 3,100 people reimbursed to date. Refunds are expected to increase as Nissan Motor Acceptance Company continues auditing dealerships statewide through 2026.
Examples from the investigation included excessive markups and charges that should not have appeared on customer bills. One customer was billed about $3,200 for recall work that federal rules require be provided free of charge. In another instance, dealership records showed electrical tape valued at just 8 cents but charged to the buyer at $2,563. Some Certified Pre-Owned repairs consisted of minimal work such as washing a vehicle but still cost customers over $2,500.
Investigators said these practices undermine consumer confidence because lease buyouts are supposed to offer clear pricing based on contract terms agreed upon at the start of the lease period. When dealers add vague or inflated line items or bill for services meant to be free or low-cost, it increases overall expenses—especially if customers finance those amounts and pay interest on them.
Affected consumers do not need to submit claims; Nissan Motor Acceptance Company is conducting audits and issuing refunds automatically across New York State. According to state officials, these payments will also cover any interest incurred by buyers who financed improper charges during their lease buyout process.
With audits continuing through 2026 and additional overcharges likely being identified during this period, authorities expect more drivers may receive refunds for illegitimate fees added by certain dealerships.
